stories.title: Multi-Agency Centre expands tracking to radicalisation hotspots
stories.summary: The Multi-Agency Centre, a centralised intelligence-sharing platform operating under the Intelligence Bureau, now tracks radicalisation hotspots alongside its existing focus on cybersecurity and organised crime. The network was revamped in 2025 to connect all police districts in the country through a secure, centralised grid.

stories.title: Amit Shah says Kashmir is free of India-born terrorists
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared Kashmir free of India-born terrorists for the first time in 35 years following the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Lateef Bhat. The minister termed the development a significant milestone in the region, which has seen over three decades of militant activity.

stories.title: BJP cites Moily remarks to claim UPA-era bias
stories.summary: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi claimed that allegations against Narendra Modi and Amit Shah during the UPA era were politically motivated, citing recent remarks by former Union Minister Veerappa Moily. Moily had commented on the judicial process and the externment of Shah during the Sohrabuddin Sheikh encounter case.

stories.title: Justice Varma says removal proceedings ended with resignation
stories.summary: Justice Yashwant Varma has informed the Lok Sabha Secretariat that his resignation renders pending removal proceedings infructuous. In a letter to the Secretary General, Varma asserted that any further attempt to remove him from office would lack constitutional foundation and maintained his innocence regarding allegations of financial misconduct.

stories.title: Justice Varma letter circulated to MPs
stories.summary: The letter from Justice Yashwant Varma regarding his resignation and the status of his removal proceedings was circulated among members of Parliament on Thursday. The document addresses the inquiry committee report commissioned by the Lok Sabha Speaker.

stories.title: Supreme Court denies plea to return Azam Khan to jail
stories.summary: The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the interim bail granted to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan by the Allahabad High Court in a money laundering case. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale rejected the Enforcement Directorate's request to stay the order.

stories.title: Azam Khan challenges mafia label after jail release
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan declared that the political battle in Uttar Pradesh would be a revolution fought on public issues rather than caste or religion. Following his release from Dasna jail, Khan challenged efforts to project him as a mafia figure in the state.

stories.title: Azam Khan criticises Asaduddin Owaisi
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan directed a remark at Asaduddin Owaisi amid competition for Muslim votes in Uttar Pradesh. Khan described the AIMIM leader as a barrister rather than a Maulana.

stories.title: FIR classifies J&K police deaths as terror attack
stories.summary: An FIR has been registered for a terror attack following the deaths of two police officers in Jammu and Kashmir. The officers, Rashpal Kumar and Babi Chand, were found dead after disappearing during a patrol. The BJP stated the incident demolished the Congress narrative on regional security.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi addresses youth leader label at 56
stories.summary: At a University of Chicago event, Rahul Gandhi responded to a question regarding his status as a youth leader at age 56. The Congress leader dismissed the inquiry as a ridiculous question while discussing his political approach.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi discusses election integrity claims
stories.summary: At a University of Chicago event, Rahul Gandhi addressed questions regarding why the opposition does not boycott elections if they believe the process is rigged. The Leader of Opposition offered what he described as nuance and referenced claims from the 2014 election cycle.

stories.title: Congress to begin UP campaign on Constitution Day
stories.summary: The Congress party plans to launch its Uttar Pradesh election campaign on Constitution Day. Priyanka Gandhi is expected to oversee seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party, with a joint campaign anticipated once the division of constituencies is formalised.

stories.title: Odisha prepares for cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: The Ministry of Communications has activated roaming facilities in coastal districts as Odisha prepares for cyclone Akvan. Officials have identified nearly 1,000 landslip-prone areas, and disaster management teams are positioned to manage the storm, which is expected to bring wind speeds of up to 110 kmph.

stories.title: Odisha evacuates 3 lakh people ahead of cyclone
stories.summary: Odisha has evacuated nearly three lakh people as severe cyclonic storm Akvan approaches the coast near Gopalpur. The state has deployed 60 units of the Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force and 14 units of the National Disaster Response Force to manage the expected landfall and subsequent restoration efforts.

stories.title: Odisha sets up 9,000 shelters for cyclone Akvan
stories.summary: The Odisha government has established 9,299 shelters and evacuated over one lakh people as cyclone Akvan approaches. Chief Secretary Anu Garg stated that educational institutes are closed and tourists are prohibited from coastal areas, with the government prioritising zero casualties during the storm's landfall.

stories.title: Red alert issued for 11 districts as Akvan nears
stories.summary: Odisha has evacuated 46,700 people as severe cyclonic storm Akvan moves across the Bay of Bengal. A red alert is in place for 11 districts, with landfall expected between Andhra Pradesh and Puri. Officials are monitoring the storm's trajectory as its speed and direction continue to shift.

stories.title: Two pilgrims killed in Kanpur bus accident
stories.summary: Two pilgrims were killed and 27 injured when a tourist bus rammed into a truck on the Etawah-Kanpur highway. Police suspect the driver fell asleep at the wheel while returning from a temple visit. The victims were residents of Unnao.

stories.title: Fire safety welding triggers fatal Delhi blaze
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man was killed and another critically injured after a fire broke out in a Lajpat Nagar basement office. The fire was triggered by welding work intended to install fire safety equipment. Police received reports of people trapped inside the four-storey building on Wednesday.

stories.title: Two killed in collision near Delhi's Kashmere Gate
stories.summary: Two people died and six were injured after a Fortuner collided with an auto-rickshaw on Yudhishthir Setu. The accident occurred on the night of November 17. Eight people were initially hospitalised, with two succumbing to their injuries on Wednesday. Police have registered an initial FIR.

stories.title: Three killed in house fire in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: A 32-year-old woman and her two daughters, aged 13 and 11, died after a fire broke out at their home in Shamli district on Wednesday night. Authorities suspect an LPG cylinder blast triggered the blaze, though the exact cause remains under investigation.

stories.title: Nine arrested for killing woman over witchcraft suspicions
stories.summary: Nine people were arrested for the abduction and murder of a 58-year-old woman in Bihar’s Jamui district. Police said the suspects targeted the woman over witchcraft suspicions following a boy’s death. Her body was discovered buried in sand on a riverbank.

stories.title: Stalker killed by family after forcing entry into home
stories.summary: A man died after being assaulted by a family and their neighbours while allegedly attempting to force his way into a social media influencer's home in east Delhi. Police have arrested the woman's father and a neighbour in connection with the November 7 incident.

stories.title: Six police officers suspended in Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav suspended six police officers, including an additional superintendent, after a video surfaced showing them threatening a couple with a false drug case. The officers allegedly demanded the couple unlock their mobile phones during a hotel raid in Seoni district.

stories.title: JD(U) demands action after minister pushed by security
stories.summary: The Janata Dal (United) has requested an investigation after Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary’s security staff allegedly pushed health minister Nishant Kumar during a visit to Vaishali. Police have described the incident as a human error, while the party seeks to determine if the move was deliberate.

stories.title: A2B secures $180 million investment from Bodhi Tree
stories.summary: Food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan has secured $180 million from Bodhi Tree Systems, a firm backed by James Murdoch and Uday Shankar. The 50-year-old brand sold a majority stake in the deal, which reportedly values the company at $350 million. Funds are earmarked for market expansion.

stories.title: Two arrested in PayU cloud server fraud
stories.summary: Gurugram police arrested two men for facilitating a cyber fraud involving the breach of PayU cloud servers, resulting in a loss of over 25 crore rupees. The suspects allegedly provided bank accounts to cybercriminals who siphoned the funds. The masterminds were arrested in Ludhiana.

stories.title: Students' fruit harvesting invention moves to commercialisation
stories.summary: Students from Coimbatore Public School developed a fruit harvesting toolkit for coffee cherries, which has now been licensed to a start-up for commercial production. The device uses a V-shaped blade system and a hollow pipe to increase the speed and efficiency of plantation harvesting operations.

stories.title: Adani Group CEO calls for self-reliance in education
stories.summary: Adani Group CEO Robin Bhowmick stated that India’s development relies on skill development and domestic production. Speaking at a conference in Vijayawada, he urged youth to adapt to automation and technical training, framing self-reliance as the primary driver for the nation’s future economic progress.

stories.title: PM Modi urges industry to compete globally
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi told industry leaders that an assured domestic market of 1.4 billion people should not lead to complacency. Speaking at a FICCI convention, he encouraged companies to look beyond local comfort zones and seize global opportunities unlocked by recent free trade agreements.

stories.title: PM Modi questions industry on jobs and wages
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi challenged industry leaders at a FICCI convention to demonstrate the impact of corporate tax cuts. He questioned whether companies had used the government's concessions to increase employee salaries or expand their workforce, noting that corporate tax rates were reduced from 30 percent to 22 percent.

stories.title: PM Modi criticises industry appetite for concessions
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi questioned industry leaders on their commitment to job creation and salary hikes despite government tax cuts. He remarked that the corporate appetite for concessions remains unsatisfied, citing reductions in corporate tax and GST as measures intended to improve the business environment.

stories.title: PM Modi critiques industry performance on wages and jobs
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised industry leaders for failing to improve manufacturing standards, increase wages, or expand employment. He also noted a trend of exporters sending high-quality goods abroad while neglecting domestic needs. The Congress party described the Prime Minister's remarks as a sign of nervousness.

stories.title: PM Modi asks industry to share tax cut benefits
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi questioned whether corporate tax cuts from 30 percent to 22 percent had resulted in higher salaries or more jobs. Speaking at a FICCI convention, he urged industries to ensure that government-provided tax relief reaches employees rather than remaining within the corporate sector.

stories.title: Congress responds to PM Modi's critique of India Inc
stories.summary: The Congress party responded to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s remarks on stagnant wages and low job creation, arguing that the government’s own policies are responsible for current economic challenges. General secretary Jairam Ramesh stated the Prime Minister is echoing concerns that the opposition has raised for years.

stories.title: PAC labels Green India Mission a failure
stories.summary: The Public Accounts Committee reported that the Green India Mission has failed to meet its targets. An audit showed only 5.3 percent of the approved area was covered by 2025, seven years past the 2018 deadline. The committee has requested the government establish a new implementation timeline.

stories.title: Supreme Court quashes mining land acquisition in Odisha
stories.summary: The Supreme Court struck down a land acquisition process for limestone mining in Odisha, ruling that prior consent from the local Gram Sabha is mandatory. The court held that the acquisition for Dalmia Cements Bharat Limited violated the 2013 land acquisition act regarding tribal rights.

stories.title: Karnataka high court orders state-wide forest survey
stories.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed the state government to conduct a comprehensive, scientific survey to identify all non-notified and unclassified forest areas. The exercise must cover the entire state, regardless of land category or region. The court issued the order after hearing petitions from various landowners.

stories.title: Supreme court clarifies highway demolition rules
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that its April order on removing unauthorised structures along national highways is not a blanket justification for demolitions. The court directed property owners to challenge individual notices in high courts, which must independently examine the legality of each structure. Road safety is not a permit.

stories.title: Sub-committee to assess Kamala hydroelectric project impact
stories.summary: The Union environment ministry has formed a three-member sub-committee to evaluate the 1720 MW Kamala Hydroelectric Project in Arunachal Pradesh. The project requires diverting over 3,200 hectares of forest land and felling 2.34 million trees and bamboo. The committee will study the environmental and social implications of the dam.

stories.title: Elephant linked to 16 deaths tranquilised in Chhattisgarh
stories.summary: Forest officials have tranquilised and radio-collared an elephant blamed for 16 deaths in Chhattisgarh over the last seven months. The tusker, known locally as Kabra Kaan, was released back into the forest after the operation. Human-animal conflict in the state continues to rise.

stories.title: Poisoning suspected in death of three leopards
stories.summary: Wildlife officials in Jammu and Kashmir have filed an FIR after three leopards, including two cubs, were found dead in the Kunzar area. Autopsies raised suspicions of poisoning. The bodies were discovered with no visible injuries, and the department is currently investigating the circumstances of the deaths.

stories.title: Rescued orangutan babies recover from anaemia
stories.summary: Five orangutan babies rescued from a forest in Odisha have recovered from anaemia, according to state officials. The infants, allegedly abandoned by wildlife smugglers in September, have regained their appetite and are showing steady health improvements. Their haemoglobin levels have returned to normal ranges.

stories.title: Naini Lake duck population declines as rats target eggs
stories.summary: The duck population at Naini Lake has dropped to fewer than 15 birds, down from over 100 a decade ago. Officials attribute the decline to rats preying on eggs and disrupting breeding cycles. Municipal authorities are now exploring measures to control the rat population and protect the remaining birds.

stories.title: Evening brief: Cyclone Akvan and Myanmar genocide ruling
stories.summary: Cyclone Akvan is expected to make landfall tomorrow along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast. Meanwhile, the International Court of Justice has issued a ruling on Myanmar regarding the 2017 Rohingya crackdown. Global leaders also released a peace declaration following a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen.

stories.title: Leaders issue peace declaration in Shenzhen
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russia's Vladimir Putin met for the first time to discuss nuclear risks and conflict resolution. The resulting peace declaration addressed UN reforms and fuel supplies but omitted mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Symbolism remains the primary output.

stories.title: Superpowers meet to discuss global reforms
stories.summary: Leaders from the U.S., China, and Russia met in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear risks and market fuel supplies. The meeting was described as historic by the participants, though no major breakthroughs were announced. The three nations agreed on the need for UN reforms and continued dialogue.

stories.title: Trump concludes Asia tour
stories.summary: President Trump has returned to Washington following an Asia tour that focused on personal diplomacy and high-profile summits. The administration defined the trip's success through the spectacle of the meetings rather than specific policy agreements. The president now faces a domestic political landscape shaped by recent midterm elections.

stories.title: Trump comments on Iran tensions
stories.summary: President Trump stated that the U.S. will assess the situation with Iran after January 1. The remarks followed reports of a potential dirty bomb threat in Washington. Trump described the Iranian leadership as nasty while alternating between threats of escalation and suggestions of winding down hostilities.

stories.title: Malaysia to end visa-free entry for Indians
stories.summary: Malaysia will terminate its visa-free entry facility for Indian nationals starting January 1, 2027. Travelers must obtain a visa through the MyVISA online portal beginning December 1, 2026. The Immigration Department of Malaysia announced the policy change in a notice issued on November 17.

stories.title: India criticises Pakistan at UN security council
stories.summary: India accused Pakistan of misusing the Indus Waters Treaty for propaganda during a UN Security Council meeting. India's Permanent Representative to the UN, Parvathaneni Harish, alleged that Pakistan's military loots natural resources for personal gain. The session focused on the intersection of natural resources and conflict.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi critiques India's foreign policy
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi stated that India has become a side player in global affairs. Speaking at the University of Chicago, he cited Pakistan's role in facilitating U.S.-Iran talks as evidence of India's declining influence. He argued that India should be more actively involved in global conversations.

stories.title: India monitors Shenzhen trilateral summit
stories.summary: The Indian government is observing the trilateral meeting between the U.S., China, and Russia with strategic caution. While there has been no official response to the summit, officials are evaluating the potential impact on India's diplomatic relations. The meeting involved leaders from the three global powers.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO net worth increases after IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's net worth rose to an estimated $19.8 billion following the company's stock market debut. The IPO valued the AI firm at $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. Amodei's stake in the company is now valued at approximately $19.6 billion.

stories.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 per share
stories.summary: Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 per share, exceeding the initial range of $70 to $78. The company increased its offering to 980 million shares ahead of its Nasdaq debut. The final price does not guarantee the cost for retail investors when trading begins.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO prices at $83
stories.summary: Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, exceeding its earlier $70 to $78 range. While $1,000 covers 12 shares, the company notes that having the funds does not guarantee an allocation. Retail investors were required to request shares through participating brokerages before the offer period closed.

stories.title: Anthropic stock begins trading on Nasdaq
stories.summary: Anthropic is scheduled to debut on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on November 19. While the market opens at 9:30 a.m. ET, brokerage Alpaca expects the first trade between 10 a.m. and noon. The $83 IPO price does not guarantee retail investors will receive shares at that rate.

stories.title: Palo Alto Networks to acquire Applied Compute for $4.5 billion
stories.summary: Applied Compute has agreed to be acquired by Palo Alto Networks for $4.5 billion. Founded 18 months ago, the startup focused on proprietary model security and auditability. The founder stated that joining the cybersecurity firm will help the company scale its efforts to keep models under customer control.

stories.title: Rockstar Games developers express job security concerns
stories.summary: Despite working on the world's largest game, Rockstar Games employees report uncertainty regarding future employment. Industry-wide, an estimated 24,000 roles have been cut over the last two years. Staff noted that while no specific layoffs have been announced, the broader trend of workforce reductions remains a persistent concern.

stories.title: Rockstar India roots trace back to Bengaluru
stories.summary: Rockstar Games' current success includes its India-based operations, which originated from the Bengaluru studio Dhruva Interactive. Rockstar acquired the studio and its 300 employees in 2019. The founder described the sale as both a loss and a validation for the team that started in a small office.

stories.title: Modi compares India development to GTA release gap
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the launch of GTA VI to highlight national infrastructure upgrades. He noted that while Rockstar Games took 13 years to release a sequel, India has undergone significant development since the 2013 release of the fifth edition. The post served as a national scoreboard.

stories.title: AI tools offer GTA 6-style image filters
stories.summary: Following the global release of GTA VI, social media users are using AI prompts to convert photographs into video game-style posters. The game, which reportedly cost over $1 billion to produce, arrived 13 years after its predecessor. The aesthetic has become a popular trend across various online platforms.

stories.title: Sarvam AI faces criticism over model access
stories.summary: Sarvam, a company that claims to provide sovereign AI, has faced criticism for selling access to Chinese models. The firm built its frontier model with support from the government's IndiaAI Mission, raising questions about the nature of its underlying technology and its alignment with national objectives.

stories.title: COP31 draft omits fossil fuel transition
stories.summary: The latest COP31 draft agreement contains no mention of fossil fuels, drawing criticism for potential backsliding. Negotiators pointed to language regarding an irreversible transition to low emissions as evidence of commitment. The nearly 200 nations involved have until Friday to finalize the text during ongoing climate talks.

stories.title: COP31 climate draft drops fossil fuel language
stories.summary: Australia, the co-host of COP31, released a slimmed-down draft agreement that removes all references to fossil fuels. The document follows days of tense negotiations among 200 nations. The final text remains under discussion as the marathon talks approach their deadline, with competing positions on energy and finance.

stories.title: Researchers model sea level rise in Los Santos
stories.summary: Scientists from the University of Potsdam and the Alfred Wegener Institute used a fan-built 3D model of Los Santos to simulate rising sea levels. The study tracked how water would impact in-game infrastructure like sewage plants and canals. The project coincided with the release of GTA VI.

stories.title: Karnataka introduces antimicrobial resistance action plan
stories.summary: The Karnataka Department of Health and Family Welfare has launched a state-level action plan to address antimicrobial resistance. The initiative focuses on surveillance, infection prevention, and One Health collaboration. The plan aims to strengthen stewardship across medical colleges and district health services to combat growing resistance threats.

stories.title: Health ministry proposes antimicrobial regulation
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed an amendment to the 2019 New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules. The change would classify antimicrobials as new drugs to increase regulatory oversight of quality and safety. The move is intended to address the global public health concern of resistance.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh plans robotic surgery in teaching hospitals
stories.summary: The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare plans to introduce robotic surgery in government teaching hospitals. A center is proposed for Vijayawada at a cost of ₹45 crore, with subsequent facilities planned for Visakhapatnam and Kurnool. The initiative is part of a phased expansion of advanced medical procedures.

stories.title: Stipend parity approved for foreign medical graduates
stories.summary: The Directorate General of Health Services has approved stipend parity for foreign medical graduates interning at five government institutions. These graduates will now receive remuneration equal to Indian medical graduates. The order, issued on November 16, applies to those undergoing compulsory rotatory medical internships at the specified centers.

stories.title: Central hospitals to pay foreign medical graduates
stories.summary: The Centre has approved a monthly stipend of Rs 30,070 for foreign medical graduates completing internships at five government hospitals. The decision brings their pay in line with Indian medical graduates. This follows the National Medical Commission's 2021 regulations regarding compulsory rotating medical internships.

stories.title: Assam medical college withdraws marriage deferral order
stories.summary: The Department of Medicine at Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an order advising postgraduate trainees to defer marriage until their residency ended. The head of the department rescinded the advisory hours after it was issued, following a backlash from a doctors' body.

stories.title: Assam medical college rescinds marriage advisory
stories.summary: A department at Assam Medical College and Hospital withdrew an order asking postgraduate trainees to postpone marriages during their residency. The directive sparked controversy shortly after its release. National Medical Commission regulations currently allow postgraduate students to take maternity and paternity leave during their training period.

stories.title: CMC Vellore hosts diabetes awareness events
stories.summary: The Department of Endocrinology at CMC Vellore will hold essay and painting competitions for students and a quiz for teachers on November 21. The event aims to promote diabetes awareness and healthy lifestyle practices as part of a community outreach initiative. The hospital is located in Vellore.

stories.title: GITAM hosts national nursing research conference
stories.summary: The GITAM Institute of Nursing has begun a two-day conference focused on qualitative and mixed-method research. The event aims to build research skills among nursing professionals and students through sessions on topics including publication ethics and scientific writing. The third edition of the conference is currently underway.

stories.title: Four companies partner for second Vikram-1 flight
stories.summary: Skyroot Aerospace is collaborating with Exolaunch, OhmSpace and HEX20 for the second Vikram-1 orbital flight. The partnership combines capabilities in launch services, satellite development and in-space propulsion. Skyroot will provide the launch vehicle and a satellite, while partners contribute deployment systems and additional payloads for the mission.

stories.title: AERB approves first approach to criticality for RAPP-8
stories.summary: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board has granted permission for the First Approach to Criticality of the Rajasthan Atomic Power Project Unit-8. The approval follows a safety review of the reactor design, construction and testing results. The project marks a stage in the commissioning of the unit.

stories.title: Shekhar Mande appointed to UN sustainable development panel
stories.summary: Indian scientist Shekhar Mande has been appointed to a United Nations panel focused on sustainable development. The appointment follows his career in the scientific community.

stories.title: UNFPA estimates India population at 1.47 billion
stories.summary: India remains the most populous country with a 2026 population estimate of 1.47 billion, according to the UNFPA. The report suggests the population will grow to 1.7 billion before declining in 40 years. More than one in four Indians are currently aged 10 to 24.

stories.title: DMRC references GTA 6 in social media post
stories.summary: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has joined the launch buzz surrounding the video game Grand Theft Auto VI. The corporation shared a post on X contrasting the game's fictional Vice City with the Delhi Metro. The post frames the transit network as a local alternative to the game.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu Police release GTA-themed anti-drug posters
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Police shared anti-narcotics posters using Grand Theft Auto-style artwork following political criticism from DMK chief M K Stalin. Stalin had previously compared the state to the fictional Vice City. The police posters highlight recent drug seizures and arrests made by the department.

stories.title: Madras High Court judge calls for constructive political discourse
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan of the Madras High Court stated that political criticism between TVK and DMK supporters should remain constructive. The judge noted that discourse should not include sexually explicit or incestuous material. The court made the observation while hearing petitions regarding objectionable social media posts.

stories.title: Police officers participate in badminton tournament
stories.summary: A total of 38 teams are participating in a badminton tournament featuring police officers. The event focuses on competition among the participants.

stories.title: Toll plazas send insurance renewal reminders
stories.summary: Toll plazas have begun sending insurance renewal messages to drivers. The initiative addresses the number of vehicles currently operating on Indian roads without valid insurance coverage.
